What's Changed

  • fix(secrets): resource reads stop trusting a user-set specName tag, and specName is reserved (swamp-club#3684) (#3386)

Summary

readResource resolves vault references only in the fields a record's _swamp.sensitiveFields tag names. For a record without that tag, it fell back to the schema of the resource spec named by the record's specName tag. Workflow tags, --tag and data output overrides could all overwrite specName. A forged specName pointing at a sensitiveOutput or schema-sensitive spec made reference-shaped text in an ordinary field resolve to the reader's vault plaintext. A file record under a file spec sharing a sensitive resource spec's name did the same.

  • _swamp.kind stamp. Both data writers set _swamp.kind (resource or file) after every user tag source has been applied. The _swamp. prefix refuses it from all of those sources (swamp-club#3635), so only the writer can set it. The new RECORD_KIND_TAG lives in src/domain/models/data_writer.ts.
  • Reader gate. getSensitiveFieldsForResolution still reads a present sensitive-fields tag first and strictly. Without one, a stamped record had nothing vaulted, so nothing resolves; its specName and type are never consulted. Only an unstamped record, written before this change, takes the schema fallback, and only when its type tag is resource. The worker shares createResourceReader, so both executors behave alike.
  • specName reserved. The new `RESERVE

  • feat(secrets): typed secrets at every internal entry point, refusals keep their codes and hold on replay (swamp-club#3735) (#3343)

Summary

Phase 4.6 of the typed-secrets design: vault.get returns a reference-only Secret at every internal entry point (CLI runs, workflows, serve, validation), with values loaded only at delivery.

  • Removes the internal typedSecrets option and the regex vault rewriting; one evaluator handles plain and secret expressions, so plain CEL is unchanged.
  • Refuses operations that would expose a secret (size, ==/in on containers, type conversion, interpolation of a container holding a secret into text) with stable codes: secret_operation_unsupported, secret_destination_refused, secret_reference_invalid, secret_reference_unavailable. The codes survive the run and serve error wrappers.
  • Behavior evaluation is a partial evaluation: a refused expression keeps its authored text, evaluate --all continues, and a --last-evaluated run re-checks what the selected method still needs, so a refused method refuses on replay instead of delivering literal text. A missing input binding on replay now fails validation instead of running literally.
  • Validation reports "Secret usage" findings with file, path, line and column, including literal containers carrying a vault.get result that are interpolated into text. Whole-field containers remain structured arguments.
  • Persisted sensitive form moves to version 3 with relia

The typed-secrets accessor adapter (adaptDataRecord and its callers) decided own versus foreign by comparing a record's namespace with the reader's exactly. So on the typed path such a row's tagged fields reached CEL as stored reference text, not as data-origin Secrets. That happened through wildcard reads such as data.latest('*:db', …) and through data.query (typed-secrets 4.3, swamp-club#3732, which landed while this PR was open). Unprefixed accessors filter ns == own, and model-map records are stamped with the repository's namespace, so neither was affected.

Other notable changes

Aa refused push drops the dirty marks it leaves, so a later push no longer deletes the new lock holder's versions; the v3 restore watch spaces its failures, takes SWAMP_V3_RESTORE_PROBE_MS, and lists nothing after a failure not about storage (swamp-club#4091, swamp-club#4092) (#3466)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-28T23:53:25Zdatastorefix

What's Changed

  • fix(datastore): a refused push drops the dirty marks it leaves, so a later push no longer deletes the new lock holder's versions; the v3 restore watch spaces its failures, takes SWAMP_V3_RESTORE_PROBE_MS, and lists nothing after a failure not about storage (swamp-club#4091, swamp-club#4092) (#3466)

Summary

swamp-club#4091. A push refused because its model lock was lost discards the refused versions and restores the datastore's copy. But the marks those writes left stayed: the save's mark on the data-name directory, the version directory and the latest marker. The S3/GCS push walks a marked directory and deletes every remote file the cache lacks. So a later bare push from that checkout deleted the new lock holder's other versions and uploaded a stale latest marker over theirs.

  • DatastoreSyncService gains an optional clearDirty(relPaths) with a written contract: exact keys only, only marks made before the call, bulk and overflow marks kept, nothing remote touched.
  • discardRefusedVersions calls it for each data name whose restore matched the datastore throughout. Any failed read, write or sync, or an unreadable latest marker, keeps that name's marks.
  • Not fixed for users yet. @swamp/s3-datastore and @swamp/gcs-datastore don't implement clearDirty yet. Until they do, a refusal warns once, naming the data names whose marks stay and saying a later push from this checkout can delete or overwrite the other run's versions there.
Docs changed: design/enablers/datastore-litestream.md, design/enablers/datastores.md

Aa serve-mode copy resets when the member's read access changes, so a widened or narrowed grant refreshes what it holds (swamp-club#4089) (#3464)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-28T22:30:23Zdatastore-v3feat

What's Changed

  • feat(datastore-v3): a serve-mode copy resets when the member's read access changes, so a widened or narrowed grant refreshes what it holds (swamp-club#4089) (#3464)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#4089. A team member's serve-mode copy was reset only when their token changed. A widened grant never brought back the compacted records it now allowed, and a narrowed grant left records the member could no longer read in their copy and files.

  • Serve sends x-swamp-datastore-access on every authenticated datastore reply, refusals included. It is a SHA-256 over:
  • the principal, its collectives and IdP groups, and its groups in the policy snapshot;
  • every grant for those subjects that names read or admin, reduced to the fields a decision reads;
  • serve's restricted behavior types.

Other subjects' grants and timestamps are left out, so a reload that doesn't touch the caller keeps it. The fingerprint is cached per snapshot and caller, and taken before the reply is answered, so a reload mid-reply shows up as a change on the next reply.

  • The client records the access the copy was built under and the access serve sent. A mismatch sticks until a reset, so replicas that disagree can't hide it. The command that sees the change warns once, and the next command resets the copy through the token-switch path. The reset gives the copy a new id, so the checkout's files are rebuilt.
  • Edges:
  • unlanded writes defer the reset instead of being refused

What's Changed

  • feat(describe): report each method's kind and whether it was declared, inferred or neither (swamp-club#4007) (#3463)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#4007.

Each methods[] entry in describe output now carries:

  • kind: create, read, update, delete, list or action, left out when no kind resolves
  • kindSource: declared (set on the method), inferred (from the method name alone) or none

This lets an agent's permission hook auto-allow read and list methods without keeping its own list of which methods are safe.

  • Domain: resolveMethodKind() in src/domain/models/model.ts wraps inferMethodKind(). The reported kind is therefore always the one swamp acts on for pre-flight checks (isMutatingKind).
  • Shared output: toMethodDescribeData() adds the fields. That covers behavior/model type describe (full and --compact), behavior get, method describe, behavior create and serve's model.type.describe.
  • Log mode: the kind shows dimmed next to each method name, e.g. probe (read) or get (read, inferred). Nothing is shown when there is no kind.
  • Docs: the swamp skill's behavior reference and design/primitives/behaviors.md document the fields. They say kind is the author's claim and isn't enforced, and that hooks should auto-allow only read and list.

Test Plan

5. Write the markers, synced when durable.

Every marker read is written, even one naming a version the cache still lacks, and no single failure stops the markers. A marker that cannot be read is skipped. Summary

Fixes swamp-club#4017, the prevention half of swamp-club#3955. The v2 filesystem datastore wrote each data version with a temp file and a rename and never synced either, then moved the latest marker and wrote the catalog row. On ext4 with delayed allocation, a power cut could keep the rename, the marker and the catalog row but lose the bytes, publishing an empty raw and metadata.yaml as latest.

Durable writes are opt-in. Set durable: true in the datastore block of .swamp.yaml, or SWAMP_DATASTORE_DURABLE=1 when the block does not set it. Off by default, because each write then costs several fsyncs: roughly double the write time on a local NVMe disk, and far more on macOS (F_FULLFSYNC), network or spinning disks. Off, writes are atomic as before (they survive a process crash) but are not synced.

```yaml

datastore:

type: filesystem

path: .swamp

durable: true

```

With it on, on a v2 datastore (the filesystem backend and the local cache of a v2 extension datastore):

  • A version's metadata.yaml and raw are written through the synced atomic write, the version directory and then the data-name and model directories are synced, and only then does the latest marker move (itself written synced) and the catalog row get written. Directories are created one level at a time (`make

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#4037. Serve resolved each direct-type workflow step's definition through findByNameGlobal. For a name with no definition yet, that read and parsed every file under models/ and .swamp/auto-definitions/. It did this once before the auto-definition creation lock and again as the re-check under it, and concurrent steps with different new names each repeated both walks.   • YamlDefinitionRepository.useNameIndex attaches the index once; serve does this as it starts.
  • Only the new findByNameGlobalFromIndex reads it. Without an index it falls back to the walk.
  • Only serve's direct-type workflow resolver (src/serve/deps.ts) calls it, through a new optional name-lookup parameter on findDefinitionByIdOrName.

Aworker_enroll_phase_telemetry_test compares lookups and scans by their attributes, not the order the collector received them (swamp-club#4030) (#3422)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-27T18:58:20Ztestfix

What's Changed

  • fix(test): worker_enroll_phase_telemetry_test compares lookups and scans by their attributes, not the order the collector received them (swamp-club#4030) (#3422)

Summary

integration/worker_enroll_phase_telemetry_test.ts failed once in verify-build. A lookup's definition_scan spans came back as name_index then full_listing instead of the expected order. The test's collector uses a SimpleSpanProcessor over FetchOtlpExporter, so every span is its own concurrent export request. The port-0 collector stores each one after an async request.json(), so the received list is in scheduling order. The product code is sequential and correct, so only the test changes.

A copy of the test whose collector reversed the received batches failed at three places that depended on order:

  • Lookups: the new worker's definition_lookup spans were expected as initial then recheck, and lookups[1] was taken to be the recheck that sits under the held lock. They are now sorted by lookup_attempt.
  • Scans (the reported failure): each lookup's definition_scan children are now sorted by scan_strategy.
  • Cancel test: the initial lookup is now found by its lookup_attempt label instead of taking the first span received.

The scans run back to back, so their start times can tie. That is why the sort uses attributes, not timestamps.

Testing

  • With the fix, the reversed-order copy and a copy that shuffles the received batches randomly both pass

What's Changed

  • fix(cel): data.version() takes a whole-number double, so data.latest(...).version - 1 works (swamp-club#3816) (#3417)

Summary

A data record's version field, and each element of data.listVersions(), reaches CEL as a double (cel-js types JS numbers as double), but data.version() was registered only with an int version. The natural previous-version expression

```

data.version("sh", "result", data.latest("sh", "result").version - 1)

```

passed swamp workflow validate (the argument is dyn at check time) and then failed at run time with found no matching overload for 'CelDataNamespace.version(string, string, double)'. It has been int-only since it was first registered, so this is a bug, not a regression.

  • Double overloads. CelDataNamespace.version(string, string, double) and version(string, string, list<dyn>, double) are registered beside the int overloads in buildInternalEnvironment, through the same receiver and fromAccessor path, so the legacy, typed-secrets and check environments all get them. cel-js dispatches on the runtime type, so an int literal still takes the int overload.
  • Whole numbers only. CelDataNamespace.version refuses a version that is not a whole number (fractional, NaN, Infinity) with data.version("m", "n", 1.5): the version must be a whole number. Zero and negative whole numbers keep their existing behaviour (a missed lookup that answers null).
  • Typed-secrets inventory. Both signatures join

Aaccess-data polls export their phases as OpenTelemetry spans, so a trace query splits file scan, gate contention, pull, queue wait and snapshot build (swamp-club#4005) (#3413)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-27T17:49:39Zservefeat

What's Changed

  • feat(serve): access-data polls export their phases as OpenTelemetry spans, so a trace query splits file scan, gate contention, pull, queue wait and snapshot build (swamp-club#4005) (#3413)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#4005. Access-data polls ran with no record of where their time went. Each cycle under swamp.serve.poll (swamp.serve.poller = access_data) now exports swamp.diagnostic.<phase> spans in the access_poll area. APL can then tell whether a slow poll was dominated by:

  • a slow file scan
  • gate contention
  • a slow remote pull
  • waiting behind another snapshot build
  • the snapshot build itself

Phases:

  • poll_cycle: the parent of every other phase, so its swamp.phase.uncovered_ms is the cycle's own work. It records:
  • reload_reason: changed, pending_retry, unreadable_retry or none
  • result: applied, no_change or skipped
  • changed, only when the pull ran
  • consecutive_failures, only on failure
  • change_detection (local filesystem source): counts records, entries and unreadable entries, along with peer changes, this process's own changes excluded from them, and whether a baseline existed.
  • gate_wait (sync pull): records gate mode (opportunistic or queued), skips before the wait, attempts and whether the gate was acquired. Its outcome is:
  • ok when the gate was acquired, or when it stayed busy and the cycle skipped
  • timeout when a queued wait ran out its bound
  • cancelled

The test pairs abs[i] (the marked path) with existed[i] (whether it was on disk at the mark). The recording hook appended the path at once but appended the existence result only after an awaited pathExists. collectGarbage marks version dirs from parallel tasks, before and after each remove, so those checks can finish out of order. The arrays then fall out of step, and a removed version's last mark borrows another mark's "still on disk" result. That is the CI assertion: actual true, expected false.

The fix writes the existence result at the index abs.push returned. Test-only, no production change. The race came in with the recorder in #3361.

On a case- or normalisation-insensitive filesystem (APFS, NTFS), a put or tombstone of a key with no file of its own on disk could reach another key's file. For example, a tombstone of VPC/1 removed vpc/1's file, and a put of VPC/1 overwrote it. The guard for this was reverted from #3915, because it listed every ancestor directory for every key on every full replay, Linux included.

This brings the guard back without that cost:

  • off: nothing folds (Linux). The guard is skipped synchronously.
  • canonical: realPath gives the name on disk (APFS). The spelling on disk is read from the real path the key guards already resolved, so nothing is listed.
  • list: realPath can't be trusted (HFS+), the probe failed, or the root is on another device. The spelling on disk is read from directory listings, matched as listed or case-folded and composed (NFC). Listings are cached for one apply page.

Adatastore API uploads are reserved before they are read, never evict a lighter principal's, and need admin; catch-up and chunk reads of a behavior definition's partition are decided per record (swamp-club#3938) (#3379)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-26T17:10:09Zservefix

What's Changed

  • fix(serve): datastore API uploads are reserved before they are read, never evict a lighter principal's, and need admin; catch-up and chunk reads of a behavior definition's partition are decided per record (swamp-club#3938) (#3379)

Summary

Hardens serve's datastore API (added in swamp-club#3915, #3368). These are the six findings swamp-club#3938 collected from that PR's verification reviews.

1. Entry cap counts only unreferenced uploads. Once a commit references a chunk, it stops counting toward the principal's 20,000-entry cap, so a busy CI token is no longer locked out for the 24-hour grace window.

2. No cross-principal eviction. At the 200,000-entry global cap, room comes first from the oldest entry a commit already references, because that commit's partition still vouches for the chunk. Failing that, it comes from the oldest upload of the principal holding the most unreferenced uploads. If that principal is the caller, or ties with another, the caller is refused with 429 upload_quota_exceeded.

3. Reserve on admit, settle on record. Every upload, a PUT or a chunk a commit carries, reserves room before its bytes are read and is recorded against that reservation once stored. Reservations count toward every cap, so concurrent requests can't overshoot the quota, and every exit path cancels them. record() refuses an upload without a live reservation.

4. PUT chunks/{sha256} needs admin until swamp-club#3922, the same rule as ever

What's Changed

  • fix(datastore-v3): a replicated commits.db leaves checkpoints to Litestream, the writer's sidecar checks that its lineage restores, and a broken lineage is restarted from the writer's copy (swamp-club#3935) (#3371)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3935: a fresh clone or restore of a v3 bucket datastore failed SQLite's integrity check, on S3 and GCS, while the writer's own commits.db was intact.

Cause. Litestream 0.5.17 loses its long read transaction when a sync request on its control socket runs its setup or a checkpoint (benbjohnson/litestream#1578; fixed on Litestream main by #1579, merged 2026-10-20, not yet released). SQLite's auto-checkpoint in swamp's own connections then restarted the WAL before Litestream read its newest frames, so those writes never reached the replica. swamp hits this squarely: every write command forces a sync through the control socket. The reported replica matched: 18 of 24,050 pages held older versions of themselves (missed writes, nothing garbled), and its compacted files restored corrupt even on their own.

Changes

  • Workaround: a replicated commits.db turns SQLite's auto-checkpoint off on every connection that commits, so only Litestream checkpoints it. Non-replicated datastores keep SQLite's default. The v3 checkpoint fitness rule pins the one site.
  • Detection: the sidecar's supervisor restores its own lineage the way a reader does (the writer's last published TXID, the same integrity and schema check

Endpoints, under /api/v1/datastore/{namespace}/ and bearer-authenticated (token and OAuth modes):

| Route | Purpose |

|---|---|

| POST chunks/has | Which of the caller's hashes serve holds and the caller may reference |

| PUT / GET chunks/{sha256} | One chunk, hashed as it streams in; reads support Range |

| POST partitions/{p}/commits | One framed request: the commit envelope plus the chunks it carries |

| GET partitions/{p}/commits?after= | Catch-up |

| GET changes?cursor= | A changes feed filtered to what the caller may read |

The full design, including the authorisation table, is the new section "Team mode: serve's datastore API" in design/enablers/datastores.md.

  • no lease ops;

  • a put/tombstone table;
  • each data-version op is paired with its put;

What's Changed

  • fix(runs): share queued run index repairs (swamp-club#3857) (#3345)

When concurrent dashboard requests encounter a stale or missing run index, approvals requests each queue another full fingerprint scan behind the same rebuild. Share repairs that are still pending at the same queue position, so those readers perform one validation pass together. Readers arriving after a pass starts, or after a writer queues, receive a later pass to preserve stale-status correction.

Shared snapshot loads and repairs now own their cancellation signal: a caller can stop waiting independently, and the work stops only when every reader has left. Tests cover queued writers, external record changes, cross-instance sharing, cancellation, failures and retries.

The eight-record reproduction goes from one rebuild plus two follow-up validations (16 record stats) to one rebuild plus one validation (8 stats). This measures less duplicate filesystem work; end-to-end latency has not been benchmarked. The merged swamp-club#3856 fix already prevents retention from unnecessarily discarding the index. This change handles duplicate work when repair is still needed.

Fixes swamp-club#3857.

  • Interrupted pass: a pass that stops between removing records and updating the index is corrected by the existing count check and stat-only incremental repair, not a full rebuild.
  • design/primitives/workflows.md documents the retention behaviour.

  • text in strings, describe() and comments.
  • What counts as a field: a secret-named property, class field or const whose value is a Zod chain starting at z. Destructured names, shorthand or variable values, and keys inside callbacks stay with the line check, so they cannot cancel a marker on the field beside them.

  • Hint: one message builder serves both the pre-flight check and the rename. sudo swamp update is suggested only for a root-owned directory outside HOME. A directory the user owns gets chmod u+w <dir>. Any other owner gets sudo chown <user> <dir>. A rename refused inside a writable directory says the binary is protected (immutable flag). Root is never told to use sudo or chown.
  • Warning: after sudo swamp update into a directory owned by the user who ran sudo (SUDO_UID), the update warns that sudo was not needed.

Fixes swamp-club#3801. Found by the Phase 4 dogfood (swamp-club#3756); blocks announcing v3 on buckets.

The two bugs

1. S3 checkouts that spell the endpoint differently forked the datastore silently.

  • Cause: replicaRootOf put the S3 endpoint into the replica root (s3:<endpoint>:<bucket>:<path>), and every lineage rule trusted only a lineage under an identical root string. A clone reaching the same bucket and prefix through a proxy, a trailing slash, or the default endpoint left implicit saw an empty datastore. Its first command, even a read-only workflow approvals, then started a lineage of its own beside the writer's.
  • Fix: a ReplicaRoot value object. It still writes the root in full, but for S3 it matches on bucket and path whatever the endpoint. A lineage under a genuinely different root that would decide the state is refused for readers and writers with datastore_v3_replica_root_mismatch, naming both roots, instead of being forked. workflow approvals, run history, vault audit-trail and vault read-secret only read, so they now use the read-only context and never take the writer lease or start a lineage.

2. A hostname change blocked every v3 bucket write for about 5 minutes.

  • Cause: the replicator judged its own Litestream sidecar by hostname plu

| duration('0ns') - duration('1ns') == duration('-1ns') | false | true |

The new methods work from the total in nanoseconds and build the result with seconds and nanos at one sign, the form cel-js already gives a parsed duration or a timestamp difference. Every duration then has one stored form, so == is correct without changing it. A swamp-side operator overload isn't possible, because cel-js refuses to re-register a built-in overload. Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3693. On a v3 datastore a put recorded a file's bytes but not its mode, and the read model wrote every file through a temp file at the default mode. So:

  • an output made executable arrived as 0644 in other checkouts;
  • the writer's own small (inline-sized) files dropped to 0644 after its next command;
  • a 0600 file widened to 0644 everywhere.

What changed:

  • The put records a file access. It is executable, private or private-executable; a plain file records none. The writer takes it from the stat it already does when staging a data version's content file (rawSource). No full POSIX modes, owners or umask bits are recorded.
  • The read model applies it. The temp file gets its access before the rename, on all four write paths: a commit, the compacted base, the check after a reboot, and an unreadable record's retry. The mode is derived from what the checkout's umask gave the new file, so private never widens.
  • Kept files are corrected safely. A file the checkout-copy guard keeps for its bytes is rewritten through a temp file when its put records an access it lacks. It is never chmodded by path. Plain puts, including every commit made before this change, keep the file's mode as before.
  • The access is stored wherever the read model keeps a put's content.

Summary

A suspended workflow could resume with a different input value after earlier steps had checked or approved the original value. Inputs are now write-once for each run: resume may add an absent input or repeat an existing value, but changing a value requires a new run. Refusals identify the input keys without exposing their values and explain how to recover.

Evaluated workflow replay now uses the inputs recorded with its cache and rejects mismatches before superseding an existing run. Behavior definitions are evaluated fresh against those inputs. Cache and run persistence preserve input provenance and every own input key, including __proto__.

Nested workflows retain late vault selectors across child suspension and resume, including optional CEL expressions such as inputs.?keyName.orValue('missing'). Secrets are still loaded in the child's scope when needed. Evaluation validates coerced/defaulted inputs consistently, and malformed or unsafe legacy caches fail with recovery guidance.

Addresses swamp-club#3583.

Compatibility

Workflows that previously supplied placeholder values and replaced them on resume must use optional, absence-tolerant inputs and validate them after they arrive. Hosts sharing a datastore should upgrade together; regenerate legacy evaluated caches with the intended inputs or start a fresh run.

𝗗 release v20261020.175130.0-sha.72af7c6c𝗖𝗟 72af7c6c𝗣 #3232𝗔 lab#3606

Av3 local durability: chunks are synced before a commit names them, one torn chunk no longer wedges every checkout, and writer and format markers survive a power cut (swamp-club#3617) (#3229)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-20T17:19:39Zdatastorefix

What's Changed

  • fix(datastore): v3 local durability: chunks are synced before a commit names them, one torn chunk no longer wedges every checkout, and writer and format markers survive a power cut (swamp-club#3617) (#3229)

What this fixes (swamp-club#3617)

A power cut could leave the v3 filesystem datastore in states with no supported recovery:

1. Chunks were never synced before the commit naming them (S1). A commit could land naming a 0-byte chunk, and every command in every checkout then failed at catch-up.

2. A torn writer.json read as "no marker" (S2). It was overwritten before recovery ran, so checkouts never converged.

3. A torn or missing datastore-format.json (S3) refused every command, and the advice it gave (re-run setup) was itself refused.

4. A clean reboot (S3) reset the read model and replayed the whole history.

5. A removal undone by a power cut (S3) was never redone after compaction.

What changed

  • Chunks are durable before any commit names them. Each commit group stages its new chunks as closed temp files, syncs them in parallel (64 at a time), renames them into place, and syncs the touched shard directories once. Only then is the commit prepared or appended. Chunks this process already made durable are not synced again. Outbox recovery runs the same barrier before it lands an entry.
  • Torn chunks count as missing. A chunk stored at the wrong size is treated as absent, so writing the same content again stores it
Docs changed: .claude/skills/swamp/references/troubleshooting/reference.md

  • What ships. The map's target is written as the map writes it, version or range included, as a written-out specifier would ship. Summary

Phase 3.3 of design/enablers/typed-secrets.md, behind the internal typedSecrets evaluator option. Follows Phase 3.2 (swamp-club#3625, PR #3209) and builds on the production Secret, fault context and boundary from Phase 3.1 (#3619).

  • Sensitive-field accessors return data-origin Secret references. With the option on, data.latest, data.version, findBySpec, findByTag and model.<name>.resource return the reader's own-namespace records with every _swamp.sensitiveFields-tagged value as a data-origin Secret.   • Strict reference validation. A new reader (readSensitiveFieldsTag, parseStoredVaultReference in src/domain/models/data_writer.ts) validates the tag, its paths and each stored reference before the record enters CEL. Anything the writer could not have stored refuses with the stable, value-free code secret_reference_invalid, recorded as a fault so an absorbing operator cannot hide it. Under the star tag the adapter walks containers and requires every leaf at any depth to be absent, null or a stored reference; a container at a tagged prefix path may hold only tagged descendants.

𝗗 release v20261020.143515.0-sha.3df48e4f𝗖𝗟 3df48e4f𝗣 #3221

Aregistry reads retry transient failures with bounded backoff and show each retry (swamp-club#3656) (#3220)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-20T14:28:06Zextensionsfeat

What's Changed

  • feat(extensions): registry reads retry transient failures with bounded backoff and show each retry (swamp-club#3656) (#3220)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3656. One stalled request to the extension registry no longer fails auto-resolution or swamp datastore setup extension.

Retry policy (src/infrastructure/http/transient_retry.ts)

  • Registry reads (GET/HEAD only) retry a timeout, a connection failure, HTTP 502/503/504, or a 429 whose Retry-After is 60s or less.
  • An initial attempt plus at most 5 retries, waiting 1/2/4/8/16s with up to 25% jitter.
  • 15s per attempt and 150s in total, all in one loop with one retry count, so rate-limit and transient retries never multiply.
  • Writes (push, upload, confirm, yank, deprecate, promote) are never retried. Neither are other statuses, nor a caller's own cancellation or deadline.

Feedback to the user

  • Before each wait, one warning goes to stderr in log mode:

swamp-club registry: GET /api/v1/extensions/… timed out after 15s · retrying in 2s (retry 2/5).

  • JSON mode prints nothing extra, so stdout stays valid JSON.
  • Final errors name the method, the path without its query string, the attempt count and the elapsed time.

Archive download

  • The fetch and the body read are retried together: 120s per attempt, 300s in total.
  • The signed URL is called without identity headers.

Bundling against a copy would ship versions the committed lock doesn't record. --frozen is also the smaller change and adds no new Deno-specific machinery.

Summary

Fixes lab #3633.

A sensitive field's generated vault key is built from

<type>/<id>/<method>/<spec>/<instance>/<field>. createResourceWriter stored

each vary instance under its suffixed name (creds-us, creds-eu), but built

the vault key from the name without the suffix. So every vary instance of one

spec and data name wrote its sensitive fields to the same key. The last write

won, and every other instance's record resolved to that instance's secret. A

staging record could hand back the prod credential.

The vary suffix is now part of the key, in one of two forms

(varySuffixVaultKeySegment in src/domain/models/data_writer.ts):

| Vary suffix | Instance segment of the key |

| --- | --- |

| at most 32 lowercase letters, digits and - (us, prod-us-east-1) | kept as written: creds-us |

| anything else (Prod, a'b, x@y, ip-10-0-0-1.ec2.internal, a long ARN, JSON) | h- and the first 32 hex digits of its SHA-256: creds-h-3f9c… |

Keeping a suffix as written only works for a narrow alphabet. Characters outside

it caused new collisions or regressions, found during review and testing on this

branch:

  • sanitizeVaultKey drops @, so x@y and xy would still share a secret.
  • A ' ends the key inside its single-quoted vault.get(…) reference, so the

secret can't be read back.

Which version is audited. Resolution runs without Deno tooling (src/domain/extensions/dependency_version_resolution.ts):

1. An exact pin (1.2.3, =1.2.3, v1.2.3) is that version.

2. Otherwise, the lockfile the bundler honours: the version it records for this import, matched by equivalent range. If the lock doesn't record the import itself, the highest locked version that satisfies it. The bundler honours a lock when it finds a deno.json (or works in package.json mode); otherwise it runs --no-lock.

3. Otherwise, the registry: the highest published release that satisfies the specifier, the dist-tag's version, or latest when unpinned. For JSR, yanked versions and prereleases are skipped first, as Deno does.

The lockfile sits behind a small LockedDependencyVersions port. Its Deno adapter (src/infrastructure/runtime/deno_lockfile_reader.ts) reads deno.lock formats 4 and 5 as data and caps the file at 16 MiB. A config that isn't plain JSON reads no lock.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3564 (v3 bug hunt group 1). Whether a v3 writer is still alive was judged wrong in seven ways. One rule now decides it everywhere: the writer lease, the writer marker, the checkout sidecar (writer.checkout.json) and the commit outbox.

Each record names its writer's process identity: processHostIdentity() (the hostname plus the pid namespace), the kernel boot id, and the process start time. The start time is read over FFI, because the compiled binary may not read /proc directly. On macOS it comes from sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID), which also answers for zombies and for other users' processes. judgeRecordedProcess (src/domain/datastore_v3/process_liveness.ts) gives one of three verdicts:

  • gone: the pid is absent, a zombie, or started at a different time than recorded, or it is this process's own pid on a record whose token isn't this process's. The holder is taken over, or its checkout recovered, at once.
  • alive: the writer's checkout stays protected whatever the TTL says.
  • unknown: the record is from another host, pid namespace or boot, a boot id is missing on Linux or macOS, or the record predates this change. Only TTL plus skew and the fence apply; such a writer is never judged gone. A writer always recognises its own checkout sidecar by the fence it wrote it with, so a missing boot id never makes it skip its

What's Changed

  • fix(gc): run gc and data gc cost the same however much history is kept, and serve's automatic retention pass is bounded (swamp-club#3535) (#3178)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3535 and explains the slow pass in swamp-club#3518.

Every swamp run gc and data gc, on every datastore, cost (files deleted) × (entries kept beside them). After each deleted run or output file, cleanupEmptyParentDirs read the whole parent directory into an array just to check whether it was empty. With a large kept history, especially outputs, where one type and method share one directory, a small backlog took minutes and a large one hours. That is what made #3518's 26-minute pass slow.

  • Cleanup without listing. cleanupEmptyParentDirs removes each parent directory with a non-recursive remove, which fails on a directory that still has entries, and never lists it. What's Changed

  • fix(datastore): a discarded v3 outbox entry is fsynced, so a power cut never brings back a commit whose failure was reported (swamp-club#3506) (#3148)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3506. The v3 commit outbox removed every entry with synchronous=NORMAL.

  • Settles were fine relaxed. A settle lost to a power cut comes back, and recovery finds the commit landed and settles it again.
  • Discards were not. After a power cut, the discarded entry of a failed commit came back. The next recovery then landed it on an unchanged head, which breaks the rule that a reported failure never lands later.

The CommitOutbox port, and the unit of work's SinkOutbox, now split remove into two operations:

  • settle stays relaxed. It is used only after a commit landed: by the unit's landed path and by recovery's landed or already-landed outcomes.
  • discard is fsynced (synchronous=FULL). It covers:
  • the unit's refusal, abandon and failed-end paths;
  • the sink's owed-removal retry at close (every owed key is retried durably);
  • every recovery drop and unreadable entry;
  • the shared-outbox drop when replication starts.

Why this goes beyond the call sites the issue names: splitting the port makes every caller choose, and recovery drops are the same class of bug. Recovery drops a run entry together with its unit's dropped data commit. If a power cut kept the data drop and lost the run drop, the next recovery would land the run record on its o

Fixes swamp-club#3485.

On S3 and GCS, a run that lost its model lock refused its push and relied on a best-effort refresh pull to replace its data versions in the cache. When the datastore was unreachable, the pull failed and the refused versions stayed dirty, so the next sync pushed them. Either data from a run reported as failed reached every clone, or, after a breakglass, it overwrote the new holder's version.

The refusal now discards the versions the push would publish, before it throws:

  • Delete. Each version is deleted through UnifiedDataRepository.delete, which moves the latest marker back and fixes the catalog.
  • Restore. A removed path stays marked dirty, and the S3/GCS extensions push a marked, locally absent file as a remote delete. So each removed file, and the latest marker, is restored as the datastore holds it, read with fetchContent under a 10 s budget. A file the datastore lacks stays removed. Without the restore, a push-only sync after a breakglass would delete the new holder's same-numbered version.
  • Refresh pull. The best-effort refresh pull still runs, then the catalog is invalidated.
  • Unchanged. Error code model_lock_lost and exit code 1. The message now says the run's data was discarded. Filesystem, v3 and lock-held pushes do not change.

2026-10-14T23:40:50Zextensionsfix

What's Changed

  • fix(extensions): extensions pushed from Windows pack folders as 0755 and files as 0644, so registry scoring can read them (swamp-club#3484) (#3130)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3484, reported by @mtaylor (swamp-club) with a precise repro. Thank you!

When swamp extension push ran on Windows, every folder in the archive was packed as drw-rw-rw- (0666) and every file as -rw-rw-rw-. Windows has no POSIX modes, so Deno reports 0o666 for every file and folder, and createTarGz copied that value into each tar header. The registry scorer runs tar -xzf on Linux, which applies the archive's modes. It can't enter a folder without the execute bit, so every extension published from Windows failed scoring with No manifest.yaml found in tarball.

  • On Windows, createTarGz now records folders as 0755 and files as 0644. These are the modes a Unix push records with the usual umask.
  • On Linux and macOS it still records the real modes, including executable bits, so pushes from those systems are unchanged.
  • createTarGz takes an optional os parameter (default Deno.build.os) so the Windows path is tested on every OS.

Extensions already published from Windows stay unscored until their author pushes a new version. Their stored archives keep 0666 folders, and rescoring reuses the same archive. Fixing modes during extraction is a scorer change and belongs in swamp-club.

Test Plan

  • New test `createTarGz: packs folders 0o755 and files 0o644 on Window

  • It still tries Deno.readTextFile first. Only when that read is refused with Deno.errors.NotCapable does it run /bin/cat, or /usr/bin/cat when /bin/cat doesn't exist.

  • Only a lowercase UUID is accepted as output.

  • a plain read writes nothing;
  • a joined load belongs to the request that started it.
  • A workflow with more run records than RUN_INDEX_CACHE_MAX_RUNS is skipped, because the cache would drop its snapshot anyway. Its record files are counted first with YamlWorkflowRunRepository.countRunRecords, a listing that stops on the signal.

race is filed as swamp-club#3455.

The reproduction ran 4 writer processes for 150 s, sampling the index

each second. Before #3105, on #3105 and with this change, entries all

go stale and are healed the same way, in sweeps whenever some reader

catches a mismatch. How many stay stale at the end of a burst depends

on when the last sweep ran.

Since #3376, push reads each entry point's module graph with deno info. deno info followed a symlinked model and parsed its target. Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3374.

Indexing a new or edited extension source imported its bundle into the command's own isolate to read and validate the export. Whatever the source did at import therefore happened in every command, including listings that never use the extension:

  • a source that called Deno.exit ended the command (exit 3, empty output);
  • a source with a never-settling top-level await hung it;
  • a source that printed put its output ahead of the JSON document.

An exit or a hang repeated on every command, because the source never reached an indexed state.

Index-time imports now probe the bundle instead of loading it. A probe imports the bundle in a Deno worker and answers with plain data: the exported type, version and description, or why there is none. The type is registered lazy and is imported into the command's isolate only when it is used.

What changed

  • BundleProber port (src/domain/extensions/bundle_prober.ts) and its worker implementation (src/infrastructure/runtime/worker_bundle_prober.ts, bundle_probe_worker.ts). The worker entry point is added to the --include list in scripts/compile.ts.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3375.

parseWriterLeaseKey accepted a fence of any number of digits, while fenceKey() refuses one above MAX_FENCE (10^12 - 1):

  • A stray key wedged the lease. A _control/writer/fence-1000000000000 file made readWriterLeaseRecords throw a generic Error, so acquire, inspect, swamp datastore lock status and swamp datastore lock release --force all failed until the file was deleted by hand.
  • Unpadded keys aliased padded ones. fence-5 parsed as fence 5 but is a different key from fence-000000000005, so putIfAbsent on one did not exclude the other (a stray fence-5 made acquire skip to fence 6; a stray released-5 would have released the real fence 5).

The parser now accepts only keys of exactly FENCE_DIGITS (12) digits whose fence is from 1 to MAX_FENCE, the exact inverse of the key constructors. Every other key is ignored, as unrelated keys already were. All lease readers (readWriterLeaseRecords, renewal #check, takeover #prune) share the parser, so every entry point is fixed together. swamp itself only ever writes 12-digit in-range keys, so no existing lease changes behaviour.

The design doc's v3 writer lease section now states which keys are lease records.

This has been the case since rollbackOnFailure was added, so it is not a regression.

  • CompositeUnifiedDataRepository routes saveDeferred and finalizeVersionDeferred by data lifetime, as save does. A DeferredWriteReceipt carries no lifetime, so the composite remembers which store issued each unsettled deferred version and settles each receipt there.
  • Promotion runs persistent first, then ephemeral. It is ordered, not atomic across the two stores. Rollback attempts both stores even when one fails. A failed promotion keeps the issuing records so the rollback that follows still reaches the right store.
  • InMemoryUnifiedDataRepository catalogs a deferred version when it is promoted, so a promoted ephemeral write is visible to data queries. It releases a never-finalized allocation on rollback, and promotion gives such a version no latest marker.
  • InProcessExecutor is unchanged. With the composite no longer throwing, a failing method reports its own error.

Datastore rework Phase 4 C (swamp-club#3359, on #2865's plan). A v3 datastore's single writer now holds a fenced writer lease instead of Phase 3's FileLock, and every commit names its fence, so a writer that lost the lease (a zombie) can land nothing.

  • The lease (src/domain/datastore_v3/writer_lease.ts) is built on create-only control-plane records under _control/writer/: fence-<n> taken with putIfAbsent, a heartbeat, and a released marker. Taking over creates the next fence and never rewrites the current one, so no compare-and-swap is needed. A fence is never reused.
  • The store-wide writer fence. commits.db (schema 4) keeps the highest fence taken. Taking the lease raises it, and every append checks it inside its own transaction after the partition's rules, so a zombie's commit is refused on every partition with datastore_v3_writer_fenced.
  • Clocks never decide safety. Expiry (TTL plus a 10 s skew allowance) only decides when another writer may take over.
  • Unchanged behaviour:
  • The busy refusal keeps its message and code.
  • swamp datastore lock status|release act on the lease.
  • A dead holder on the same host is still taken over at once.
  • A live Phase 3 writer.lock refuses the lease during an upgrade.
  • **Serve takes the lease back once another writer is done.

Athe claude tool no longer hides a repo's own AGENTS.md behind a new CLAUDE.md (swamp-club#3346) (#3057)

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-13T15:26:45Zrepofix

What's Changed

  • fix(repo): the claude tool no longer hides a repo's own AGENTS.md behind a new CLAUDE.md (swamp-club#3346) (#3057)

Summary

Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when there is no CLAUDE.md. swamp init --tool claude (also the default tool) always created a CLAUDE.md. So in a repo that keeps its rules in AGENTS.md, Claude read swamp's instructions and ignored the repo's own. If you deleted CLAUDE.md, swamp repo upgrade recreated it. Fixes swamp-club#3346.

The claude tool now looks at the repo before writing and picks a target. The first rule that matches wins:

1. .claude/rules/swamp.md exists, or CLAUDE.md is a symlink: write the rules file. Symlinking CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md is a setup Claude Code's docs recommend. Swamp no longer writes through that link.

2. CLAUDE.md already holds swamp's managed section: keep writing there. If the file holds nothing else and AGENTS.md has the repo's own content, add an @AGENTS.md import inside the managed section. This repairs repos this bug already hit.

3. AGENTS.md has the repo's own content and there is no CLAUDE.md: write .claude/rules/swamp.md. Claude Code loads rules files alongside AGENTS.md, and has done since 2.0.64.

4. Otherwise: write CLAUDE.md, byte-for-byte as before.

Swamp's Claude rules never go into AGENTS.md itself. Claude Code before 2.1.277, and some sessions before 2.1.281, read only CLAUDE.md files and rules, so they would lose swamp's rules

Docs changed: design/surfaces/agent-interface.md

What's Changed

  • fix(workflows): a forEach's iterations run in list order (swamp-club#3318) (#3043)

Problem

A forEach step's iterations ran in the order of their expanded names, not their place in the in list. Within one level, TopologicalSortService.sort broke weight ties by name with localeCompare, and every iteration carries its template step's weight. So operate-10 ran before operate-2, and a step named deploy-${{ self.env }} over prod, dev, staging ran dev, prod, staging. With concurrency: 1, a workflow whose items each depend on the one before skipped every item from the tenth on.

Fix

  • GraphNode takes an optional group: { key, index }. Within a level the sort orders by weight, then the group key in place of the name, then the index, then the name. This is a single total order, so it stays deterministic and invariant under input order.
  • The execution walk groups each real forEach iteration under its template step at its list position. Iterations stay together and run in list order. Plain steps, jobs and the other sort callers set no group and sort exactly as before.
  • design/primitives/workflows.md states the within-level order.

Testing

  • Sort unit tests: 12 index-named iterations, named iterations in non-alphabetical order, iterations among plain steps, weight still ordering grouped nodes.
  • Property test: the generator now produces groups, and the ordering invariant checks the four-part order across random graphs.
  • Execut

A signal by key that arrives before the wait opens is held as the key's pending signal instead of being refused no_open_wait; a step that opens its wait within that window takes it and the run does not suspend there.

  • Protocol. The signaller stores its record and then reads the key; the step claims and registers and then reads the slot. Each writes before it reads, so one of them always sees the other.   • Idempotency keys. A signal may carry one (--idempotency-key, the Idempotency-Key header, idempotencyKey over the WebSocket). A retry by the same sender under the same key is answered with the first signal's receipt and duplicate: true, and is neither delivered nor held again, including when the copies race.
  • Authorization. A signal held through serve records the workflow name its sender was authorized under, and only a wait whose run recorded that name takes it.
  • Older clients. The server holds a signal over the WebSocket only for a request

  • A dispatch that bypasses the scheduler (skipScheduler, used by the fleet probe) no longer releases a reservation it never took.
  • design/enablers/remote-execution.md describes the reservation: a slot is counted once.

Not a regression: multi-slot workers and the counted reservation arrived together in #1769.

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3276 (moved from #3006). Before this change, if a remote-run WebSocket connect failed and the error contained no HTTP status or TLS problem, the CLI checked /health. If the server answered, it replaced the real error with Authentication failed — run: swamp auth server-login. Dropped connections, early closes and serve's own 429s were all reported as auth failures, and the real cause was lost.

Most likely cause of the reporter's loopback failures (reproduced live): all loopback calls come from 127.0.0.1, so they hit serve's per-IP burst limit of 50 per minute. Over wss://, Deno's WebSocket client negotiates HTTP/2, which hides serve's 429. The /health guess then turned it into "Authentication failed", and serve's log showed zero token rejections, matching the report.

Change (src/cli/remote_run.ts): when a handshake fails without a status, the CLI repeats the handshake once as an HTTP/1.1 request without the token and classifies the error from the status serve returns:

| Probe result | Message |

|---|---|

| no answer | original error |

| 429 / 5xx | rate-limited / server error |

| 401/403, no token sent | Authentication failed — run: swamp auth server-login … (unchanged) |

| 401/403, token sent over wss:// | same auth message plus the original error (a token rejection can hide behind HTTP/2) |

| 401/40

Adormant history compaction so superseded chunks can be reclaimed (swamp-club#3258) (#3005)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-12T02:17:01Zdatastorefeat

What's Changed

  • feat(datastore): dormant history compaction so superseded chunks can be reclaimed (swamp-club#3258) (#3005)

Summary

Datastore rework Phase 3: dormant history compaction (swamp-club#3258). Superseded content can now be reclaimed without a checkout ever needing a chunk that GC deleted.

  • Compaction point (store-wide). compactHistory(through) folds every commit at or below the point into a compacted base in commits.db, then deletes those commits. The base holds present records, live versions, catalog rows and forwards, file ownership and compacted seqs. It runs in batches of 250, one transaction each. A crash leaves each batch either whole or absent.

swamp now sends a stop request on Windows, the equivalent of SIGTERM from one swamp process to another:

  • Listener (src/infrastructure/process/windows_stop_request.ts): a named auto-reset kernel32 event, Local\swamp-stop-<pid>, polled every 100ms on an unref'd timer.
  • Each subscription has its own idempotent end.
  • A failed create leaves no state behind.
  • The event is drained once at creation, so a stale request aimed at a reused pid is ignored.
  • A handler that throws doesn't keep the request from the other subscribers.
  • registerShutdownHandler: on Windows, it listens for stop requests where it would register SIGTERM on POSIX. No call sites change.

Datastore rework Phase 3 (swamp-club#3250, tracking swamp-club#2865), dormant until the v3 opt-in. This is the first of three repository staging groups. It adds the shared typed staging route, and makes the data and output repositories stage typed changes on v3 for every write they make. v2 behaviour does not change.

1. The shared route, and why it costs v2 nothing

A repository makes two calls (src/infrastructure/persistence/unit_of_work_scope.ts):

  • Before the write: signalChange(markDirty, pathChange, { typed: true }), the same call as today.
  • On v2 the option changes nothing.
  • In a bound unit that takes typed changes, the path change is checked but not staged. A write outside a bound unit is still refused before anything is written.
  • After the write: stageTyped(markDirty, build), once per batch.
  • On v2 it returns after one requiresUnit lookup, and build never runs. The test stageTyped: a builder never runs on v2: no hook, route 2, or a legacy unit covers this.
  • On a v3 hook with no bound unit it throws UnscopedWriteRefusedError before building.

The issue sketched a single pre-write call with a lazy builder. That can't work: the version, the content and whether the latest marker moved are all only known after the write, and moving the call after the write would change v2's pre-write signal timing.

Summary

Dormant chunk garbage collection for the v3 datastore: it reclaims chunks no commit names (left by abandoned units, refused or failed commits, and crashes between storing chunks and committing), finds damaged chunks, and removes the filesystem storage's orphaned temp files. Nothing in production calls it; a v3 datastore gc wires it in at the opt-in.

The reference set is the commit log, not chunksInUse

A fresh checkout catching up from cursor 0 replays every commit and reads every chunk each put names, including content later overwritten, deleted or garbage-collected. Deleting any of those would stop the catch-up permanently with ChunkMissingError. chunksInUse describes one checkout's present records at its own cursor, so it cannot be the reference set. A chunk is kept for as long as any stored commit names it.

The chunk index and its migration

  • commits.db schema 2 adds chunk_refs(namespace, sha256), written in each append's own transaction, so a refused, repeated or rolled-back append writes none.
  • Commit.chunkRefs() / BlobRef.chunkHashes() define what a commit names: the whole-content hash for one chunk, every part's hash otherwise.

What's Changed

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3241. On Windows, Deno turns every signal into TerminateProcess, which ends one process and leaves its children running. So when swamp workflow cancel or swamp model cancel stopped a run's owner, or a supervisor stopped swamp serve, the step's powershell (running Start-Sleep) survived. The survivors held files open (os error 32 on cleanup) and serve's inherited stdout/stderr, so anything waiting on serve's output hung until the step finished.

Each shell step on Windows now runs in a kill-on-close Job Object (src/infrastructure/process/windows_job.ts, kernel32 via FFI):

  • When the swamp process dies: for any reason, its job handles close and Windows ends every step process tree. This covers cancel and serve stop with one mechanism.
  • On abort or timeout: the job is terminated after the existing taskkill /T, so the walk still starts from the live child. The job then sweeps descendants the walk can't reach.
  • When a step exits on its own: kill-on-close is cleared before the job closes, so what the step deliberately backgrounded keeps running, as on POSIX. Breakaway is allowed for programs that ask for it.
  • When a job can't be made: the step runs without one, as today.

process_kill.ts and the cancel commands are unchanged.

A new optional pullChanged input runs inside the lock and the gate before the re-read, and invalidates the catalog when anything was pulled. This follows the same pattern as the handlers' pullBeforeTokenWrite. If the pull fails, it throws before anything is deleted.
  • Design doc. design/primitives/serve.md is updated: the gap description is removed, and it now describes the lock and pull the GC takes, their cost, and what MAX_TOKENS_PER_SWEEP does and does not bound.

The code-range scanner fails toward redacting: unclosed fences and spans, escaped backticks, invalid fence openers, indented code blocks and multi-line spans are all treated as prose. Fence scanning stops at the first unclosed fence, which keeps it linear.

  • The cascade never writes the parent, and one child's failure does not stop the rest.

Backstop on the child. A suspended nested run whose parent ended, or whose parent step moved on to another child, refuses approve, reject and resume and cancels itself. Recover and signal delivery reach it through resume.

  • Validation: workflow validate refuses the same key on two steps of a workflow and a key on a step under forEach, naming the steps.

  • Claims: numbered write-once records in the control-plane store, wait-keys/<workflowId>/<key>/<generation>, created with putIfAbsent as continuation claims are. swamp serve runs every scheduled workflow through one global queue, one run at a time, and no setting changes that. On the reporter's serve, each run spends about 37 s in datastore sync. Once a per-minute schedule was added, the queue saturated: a 40 */6 * * * fire started 2 h 49 min late, and a 2-59/5 schedule ran half its fires. Health only shows running, so none of this waiting was visible.

New setting: max-concurrent-scheduled-runs. Available as a config key, the SWAMP_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS env var and the --max-concurrent-scheduled-runs flag on serve and serve daemon enable. It is separate from --max-concurrent-runs, which limits API runs.

  • Default is 1, which keeps today's behaviour: one scheduled run at a time, in fire order.
  • Above 1, the scheduler starts the first queued run whose workflow isn't already running. Different workflows run together; a workflow never overlaps itself. A cron fire (keyed by workflow id) and a replayed run (keyed by name) count as the same workflow.

Queue delay in health.

  • Each schedule in the health snapshot, /health and the dashboard now reports queued, oldestQueuedAt and lastQueueDelayMs.
  • schedule_started carries queueDelayMs.
  • All queue data is per schedule, so the per-token health view filters it along with its schedule

Asettle expired signal waits from the continuation sweep (swamp-club#3109) (#2943)

`feat` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-08T19:19:10Zservefeat

What's Changed

  • feat(serve): settle expired signal waits from the continuation sweep (swamp-club#3109) (#2943)

Summary

Under swamp serve nothing looked at a wait_for_signal deadline, so an expired wait stayed suspended and its failed handlers did not run until someone resumed the run (swamp-club#3109, split out of swamp-club#3094).

  • The continuation sweep settles expired waits. When continueSettledRun finds a run held back only by its waits, settleExpiredWaits settles each wait that is past its deadline, has no outcome and is still registered, through the write-once create. The run then continues on the path a signalled run takes, so the resume fails the step with wait_timeout and failed handlers run with no client action.
  • --max-signal-wait-timeout on serve (env SWAMP_MAX_SIGNAL_WAIT_TIMEOUT, config key max-signal-wait-timeout, at most one year). A step that asks for a longer wait fails when it would open the wait. A wait already open keeps its deadline.

Behaviour to know

  • Timeouts follow the workflow's auto-resume policy, as signals do. A workflow serve may not resume keeps its expired wait unsettled and its run suspended.
  • The sweep settles only a wait whose registration can still be read, so a suspended copy of a run that ended or was deleted elsewhere never gets an outcome.
  • Each instance reads the deadline against its own clock and the first create wins, so serve hosts need synchronised clocks. There is no skew allowance.

  • Protocol. A keyless worker sends needsGatePass. The serve replies with gatePass: the swamp-club-signed proof its own pass rests on, encoded as <proof>.<signature> with no pid. How a run is continued:

  • The instance that accepts the signal continues the run at once.
  • A sweep at boot and every --continuation-sweep-interval (default 30s, 0 disables) picks up a launch that was lost and runs signalled by a local command.
  • A continuation claim in the control plane keeps two serve instances, or an instance and a local workflow resume, from resuming the same suspension. The sweep does not start on a synced datastore that has no shared atomic claim store.
  • A resume that starts and fails is retried with a backoff from 30s to 15m, per suspension.

What serve does not continue:

  • A parent waiting on a nested run, except right after a caller with the right grant continued its child.

```
[WRN] Catalog migration to per-extension-aggregate-v3 failed (Error: database is locked …); falling back to cold-start rebuild

[WRN] Catalog cold-start rebuild complete; loaders will repopulate from disk on next access

```

runDataMigrationTransaction opened a deferred BEGIN, read the catalog, then blocked on its first write. When another process committed meanwhile, the stale WAL snapshot failed with database is locked, and busy_timeout does not retry that. The catch treated the error as a data failure: it warned and ran the cold-start rebuild, which empties the catalog. On a fresh catalog that is only noise. On a populated pre-v3 catalog being upgraded, it would wipe every row and force a full re-import.

The migration now:

  • takes the write lock up front with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, as CatalogStore already does;
  • re-checks its marker under the lock, and skips work another process committed while it waited;
  • rolls back and rethrows lock errors, so initializeWithRetry retries them with backoff, as its docs already said it did.

Only real migration failures still fall back to the cold-start rebuild.

Without managedConfig the behaviour is unchanged: one attempt, a WARN, and serve starts.

`fix` change · swamp-club/swamp

2026-10-07T22:31:15Zextensionsfix

What's Changed

  • fix(extensions): captured deno output stays plain when FORCE_COLOR is set (swamp-club#3166) (#2918)

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#3166.

The extension quality check, swamp extension fmt and the rubric scorer run deno with NO_COLOR=1 so the output they capture is plain text. Deno lets FORCE_COLOR win over NO_COLOR at any non-empty value (0 included), so a shell that sets it put ANSI escape codes into the fmt and lint issue output. That includes the issues[].output strings in the JSON from swamp extension fmt --check --json, and it failed two tests in extension_quality_checker_test.ts whenever the suite ran under FORCE_COLOR.

Leaving FORCE_COLOR out of the child's env record does not fix it: Deno.Command merges the record over the parent environment unless clearEnv is set, so the child still inherits the variable. An explicit empty value replaces the inherited one, and deno reads it as unset.

What changed:

  • New helper plainDenoEnv in src/domain/runtime/deno_plain_env.ts. It sets NO_COLOR=1, overrides FORCE_COLOR with an empty string, and drops other casings of FORCE_COLOR so the record never carries two spellings on Windows.
  • Four call sites use it in place of { ...env, NO_COLOR: "1" }:
  • the fmt and lint commands in checkExtensionQuality
  • runFmt and runLint in createExtensionFmtDeps

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#2844 and swamp-club#3162. Both bugs are in swamp datastore setup (src/libswamp/datastores/setup.ts).

swamp-club#2844: setup overwrote a remote config tier

On a managedConfig repo whose .swamp/config is the config tier, datastore setup extension copied that tier into the cache and pushed it before pulling anything. If the remote already held a config tier, for example when a second repo joins a shared datastore that was already migrated, the push overwrote the team's definitions, upstream_extensions.json and the managed-config-migrated.json sentinel. Each file went to whichever repo wrote it last.

What setup does now:

  • Pulls the remote config first. It pulls only config/ (subdirs: ["config"], with the namespace, and metadataOnly under lazy hydration) before any copy, within the setup sync timeout.
  • Stops on a failed pull, including a timeout. Nothing moves and .swamp.yaml is not rewritten. A timeout has to stop setup too: committing the new datastore without migrating would make a retry classify the tier as instance-local.
  • The remote copy wins. planConfigTierMerge, a pure function in datastore_config.ts, decides what happens to each file the local tier and the cache both hold:
  • Shared files are not copied, so they are never pushed.

Summary

A nested structural swamp (for example swamp data gc) skips the per-model locks named in its inherited lock list, on the assumption that the holder waits on it and writes nothing until it exits. That stopped being true when the hop the lock was lent to ended with something still running under it:

  • a dispatch that is cancelled before the worker has killed its runner;
  • a worker that is lost, whose step is dispatched again under the same lock;
  • a shell command that killed the --server client it started, or left a swamp in the background.

The leftover swamp kept skipping the lock while the holder wrote (swamp-club#3111). The --server path was reproduced against a loopback swamp serve; the two dispatch paths were traced in the code.

The holder cannot confirm that what it started is dead: a worker kills only the runner process, a partitioned worker confirms nothing, and a run requested over --server is meant to outlive a dropped socket. So the holder acts on its own lock instead.

Summary

A step dispatched to a worker streamed its output to the client but never to the run log. swamp workflow history logs reported "Log file not found or empty" for every remote run, and the output was gone once the live stream ended.

The run log only accepts records tagged with the run's id. A worker's method logger has no run id, and its lines came back to serve as stream events that reached only the in-memory event buffer. The worker's console capture (DispatchResult.logs) was returned and then dropped.

Changes

  • Serve persists worker output. MethodExecutionService writes each output event a worker streams back through the run logger before forwarding it. This covers workflow steps and direct model method runs, which share the code.
  • The event is worker-supplied, so its shape is checked, the level is whitelisted, and a line is split on every line separator into one record each.
  • Level preserved. The output event carries an optional level, so an error line is not recorded as a warning. A worker that predates it falls back to the stream.
  • Console capture forwarded. DispatchService turns DispatchResult.logs into output events, for a failed dispatch as well as a successful one. A listener that throws while they are forwarded does not fail the dispatch.

The problem

When a command/shell step used the same vault.get() secret more than once, swamp chose the reference form once, from the first use, and reused it at every use.

  • Single-quoted or unquoted first, then double-quoted. The double-quoted use expanded unquoted. The secret was word-split and globbed, and its fragments reached stdout and logs unredacted.
  • Double-quoted first, then single-quoted. The single-quoted use silently stayed a literal, and swamp gave no warning.

The change

  • Each vault.get() use is now placed by the quote context it sits in. On POSIX that context comes from the same comment- and here-doc-aware shell scanner that sensitive data values already use (classifyShellPositions).
  • Inside a here-document body, only the quotes earlier on the same line count. This keeps the forms main produces there.
  • PowerShell still reads the context from quote characters, now separately at each use.
  • The single-quote warning now comes from the same classification. It fires for every single-quoted use, not just the first. ShellSecretResolution gains singleQuoted, and findSingleQuotedSentinels is removed (shell_model.ts was its only caller).
  • design/primitives/vaults.md is updated. The public manual change is tracked in swamp-club#3099.

Fixes swamp-club#2983.

The orchestrator holds a step's per-model lock while a remote worker runs the step. A worker is not a descendant of the orchestrator, so a nested structural swamp started by the step on a same-host worker (for example swamp data gc against the same datastore) waited on its own step's lock until SWAMP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS and failed with exit code 75.

The dispatch now carries the lock holder:

  • Orchestrator: when it builds a remote step request inside a runHolding scope, it sends its pid, hostname and the nonces of the locks held for that run as an optional lockHolder field of DispatchParams.
  • Worker: when the hostname is its own, it puts the pid at the front of the dispatch runner's SWAMP_LOCK_ANCESTOR_PIDS and the nonces into SWAMP_LOCK_HOLDER_TOKENS. The nested swamp then skips exactly the dispatched step's locks and still waits on every other lock the orchestrator holds.
  • Validation: the field is bounded by the dispatch schema and checked again by withRemoteLockHolder, which never adds the pid without its tokens entry.
  • Compatibility: the field is optional, so REMOTE_PROTOCOL_VERSION is unchanged. An older worker ignores it and an older orchestrator never sends it.

Two parallel workflow steps, or two concurrent runs, that each start a nested structural command (swamp data gc, datastore sync, and so on) wait on each other. Each nested drain skips its own run's per-model lock and waits on the other run's, and each run keeps its lock until its nested command exits. Both used to fail at SWAMP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS.

Now one of them fails within seconds and the other proceeds.

  • Drain-wait markers. A drain that has to wait publishes a short-lived marker under drain-waits/ in the datastore. It names the locks the drain skips (held for it until it exits) and the locks it waits on, by lock-file nonce.
  • Mutual wait. Two drains wait on each other when each waits on a lock the other skips. A drain nested deeper in the same run skips those locks too, so it is waited for, not failed.
  • Who yields. Drains are ordered by start time, then id. A drain yields when it mutually waits with an earlier drain that is not itself yielding, so of a group that all wait on each other exactly one keeps waiting.
  • Confirmation. A drain yields only after seeing the same opponent on two polls with the opponent's marker refreshed in between. A stale marker, or one left by a killed drain, cannot fail a live command.

WalSink kept at most one checkpoint on its delivery queue, tracked by a flag. A checkpoint queued by replay or the timer therefore suppressed the one flush asked for, even when a segment had been queued in between. That segment was delivered after the only checkpoint, so flush and close returned with it still in the WAL. On the next start it was replayed and stored a second time, which swamp audit verify reports as a broken chain.

The same ordering made the unit test "replayed segments are delivered before events written after replay" fail intermittently (swamp-club#3081): it passed only when the delivery loop happened to run replay's checkpoint before flush was called.

  • #queueCheckpoint now skips only when the queue already ends with a checkpoint, so a checkpoint always follows every segment queued when flush, replay or the timer asks for one. The earlier checkpoint stays where it is, so segments ahead of it are confirmed as early as before.
  • The queue can now hold several checkpoints, so the prune in #enqueue also drops a checkpoint left directly behind another. A checkpoint at the head is kept, because segments already delivered wait on it. The queue stays bounded by the WAL while the downstream sink hangs.

Deno refuses every /proc path unless the process has --allow-all, which neither the compiled binary nor the test and dev tasks have. Both Linux probes in src/infrastructure/runtime/process.ts went through Deno and so never worked there:

Both now read /proc through libc over FFI (--allow-ffi is already granted), the route process_ancestry.ts takes for the same restriction. isProcessGone falls through to the SIGURG probe when the entry is absent or libc cannot be loaded.

The two fixes ship together on purpose: turning liveness on while the identity still lacked the namespace would let one container roll back another's in-flight write.

acquireModelLocks takes each per-model lock and registers it with the sync coordinator before it pulls. A throw after that point returned no lock result, so the caller had nothing to flush. The CLI was covered by the flushDatastoreSync in runCli's error path; serve has no such teardown and calls acquireModelLocks per request.

Acquisition is now all-or-nothing: any throw in the per-model loop releases the locks this call registered and rethrows the original error. That covers three paths:

  • the step-start pull failing (the reported case)
  • the global lock re-check after an acquire throwing
  • a later model's lock acquire failing after earlier locks were taken

The error text and the returned lock result are unchanged, and no caller changes. Most of the diff in src/cli/repo_context.ts is the loop body being reindented inside the try; git diff -w shows the roughly 20 lines that matter.

  • LaunchdScheduler.refresh() rewrites the plist (same binary and interval) and re-registers the job with bootout, a wait, then bootstrap. That drops the stale pin.

A forEach step over items that aren't slug-safe, such as file paths, had no way to give each iteration its own unique identifier. Because of that, it couldn't create one model definition per iteration. The engine already tracked the iteration index, but expressions couldn't read it.

This PR exposes it as self._index, the zero-based iteration index. It is available wherever self is built for a forEach iteration:

  • step-name expansion (ForEachExpansionService)
  • the step context at run time: guards, task fields, model and workflow names (WorkflowExecutionService.runStep)
  • the copy of self that DefaultStepExecutor rebuilds after model resolution, so definitions and deferred data.latest(... string(self._index) ...) inputs resolve too. This goes through the new StepExecutionContext.forEachIndex field.
  • swamp workflow evaluate (libswamp/workflows/evaluate.ts), so a dry evaluate shows the same names a real run produces

An iteration variable named _index still takes precedence, so existing workflows keep their meaning. The skill reference and design/enablers/expressions.md document the variable, the factory pattern, string() for concatenation, and scoping index-based names to the run. swamp-club#2986 tracks the manual pages.

The problem. acquireModelLocks set SWAMP_LOCK_HOLDER_PID in the process-global env when it took locks, and deleted it on flush. A nested structural swamp (e.g. swamp data gc run from a shell step) reads this variable to skip its parent's per-model lock instead of waiting on it.

Per-step workflow locks and concurrent swamp serve runs hold locks side by side in one process. The first flush therefore cleared the marker while the other runs still held their locks. A child started after that waited on its own parent's lock until SWAMP_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS, then exited 75.

Reproduction. A job of 30 parallel short steps plus one step running a nested data gc hit the timeout in 6 of 10 runs.

  • SWAMP_LOCK_ANCESTOR_PIDS (new). Published once at startup in runInvocation. It lists every swamp above a child, oldest first, ending with the publisher. A nested swamp therefore skips locks held by any ancestor, not just its parent. This keeps nesting working through a swamp that takes no locks, and through deeper chains, which used to time out.
  • SWAMP_LOCK_HOLDER_PID. Set to the process's own pid the first time it takes a lock (markHoldingLocks() from `acqui

Summary

Fixes swamp-club#2870.

FileLock doubled its retry backoff up to an 8 s cap shared by every lock. A workflow step holds its model's lock for the whole method run, so concurrent steps against one instance queue on that lock, forEach iterations for example. The waiters at the back of the queue then slept for seconds after each release.

  • Add a maxBackoffMs option to FileLock only, defaulting to 8 s. The backoff arithmetic moves into a pure nextBackoffSleep helper. Jitter is still applied before the result is clamped to the cap and the remaining time budget.
  • createModelLock() passes MODEL_LOCK_MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 250. The global datastore, extension-install, pulled-extensions and auto-definition locks keep the 8 s default. The domain LockOptions and the extension datastore-provider contract are unchanged.
  • Rewrite the "Retry backoff" section of design/enablers/datastores.md.
